propositions: A one-time backfill script must sample historical commits (default monthly), measure cyclomatic complexity via lizard and clone count via jscpd, and write snapshots to the metrics store.
Each snapshot's timestamp must be the sampled commit's date (via git show) not the backfill run time, so historical trends are correctly positioned.

The measure_tree function shells to complexity and clone tools and returns a dict with integer complexity and clone_count keys; if a tool is absent or errors, the function returns None and that commit is skipped without aborting.
All backfilled snapshots must carry source="snapshot" and confidence="high" metadata tags.
Tests must stub measure_tree output to avoid tool dependencies and verify snapshot count, integer-typed metrics, per-commit timestamps, and graceful skip behavior for failed measurements.
